verifier: Claude (Anthropic): manual reading of the pinned text. Not a human review and not an author decision.
rule: Semantic verification gate: a finding, a FAIL of a reference example, a normative conflict, a systemic blocker or an author question gets that status only after the provisions involved are read against the literal pinned text. Codex drafts are never a source. Every quote below must occur verbatim (after markdown normalization) in the named document; 'absent' records a string that must not occur.

classes.CONFIRMED_FINDING: the literal texts produce the defect (contradiction, broken reference, wrong number, missing definition) without any lab reading
classes.INTERPRETATION_GAP: the result depends on a reading or a definition the corpus does not give; no text is contradicted
classes.IMPLEMENTATION_BUG: the lab's own reading or code produced the reported defect; the texts do not
classes.UNVERIFIED_FINDING: recorded but not yet verified against the literal text (reported as such, never as a protocol defect)

quotes.text: #### 7.1 Trigger Conditions - new admissible data
Create a new evaluation event
Recompute deterministically with updated inputs
No enforcement output SHALL remain active solely based on past VALID state if:
new admissible data is introduced
Justice outputs SHALL be re-evaluated when: - impact metrics change,

findings.conclusion: New admissible data is itself a trigger (EB §7.1) and leads to a new evaluation and recomputation (EB §7.2); ETRANS §4.2 forbids keeping an output active on a past VALID state once new admissible data is introduced. The lab's former hypothesis (only declared events trigger re-evaluation) contradicted these texts. Fixed in failure_chain 1.2.0; the former reading is kept only to reproduce the old result and now fails ETRANS-4.2-01.

findings.conclusion: The 7 % threshold is stated, but not the metric between two distributions nor how classes sampled at different times are aligned. The divergences from asynchronous sampling come from the lab's point-value comparison (H-FC-3, H-FC-4).

The suspension of dependent outputs follows from the lab's mapping H-FC-1; EB §9 points the other way for stable environments.
